Create a DuckLake table

Source: R/create_table.R
create_table.Rd

Create a DuckLake table

Usage

create_table(
  data_source,
  table_name,
  labels = TRUE,
  partition_by = NULL,
  sort_by = NULL,
  options = NULL
)

Arguments

data_source

Raw data source. Can be:

  • A URL (http:// or https://)

  • A file path (e.g., "data.csv", "data.parquet")

  • An R data.frame or tibble

  • A lazy table (tbl_duckdb_connection or tbl_lazy). A lazy table on the package's connection, such as a dplyr pipeline built on get_ducklake_table(), is written with CREATE TABLE ... AS inside DuckDB, so its rows never pass through R. A lazy table on another connection is collected first.

table_name

Name of the new table

labels

When TRUE (the default), store variable labels in the lake as column comments, in the same transaction as the table creation, so both land as one snapshot. For a data frame the labels are its haven/labelled label attributes; for a lazy table, each output column keeps the comment of the same-named column in the tables the query reads, so labels follow the data through a pipeline (a renamed or derived column starts without one). Collecting the table later restores the labels (see get_table_comments()), and every other client of the lake can read them too. Set to FALSE to skip.

partition_by

Optional character vector of partition expressions, as for set_table_partitioning(): column names, year(col) and the other calendar transforms, or bucket(n, col). The keys go on before the rows, so the first load is already partitioned, where set_table_partitioning() on an existing table affects only later writes.

sort_by

Optional character vector of sort expressions, as for set_table_sorting(): a column name, optionally followed by ASC or DESC and NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST. The first load is written in this order.

options

Optional named list of table-scoped options, as for set_ducklake_option(), for example list(parquet_compression = "zstd", data_inlining_row_limit = 0). They are set before the rows are written and so govern the first load too: an inlining limit of 0 here sends even a handful of rows to a Parquet file instead of the catalog.

Value

Invisibly, NULL. Called for its side effect of creating the table in the lake.

Details

With any of partition_by, sort_by, or options, the table is created empty from the source's columns, the keys and options go on, and the rows are inserted, in one transaction (yours when one is open), so the result is one snapshot with the layout in force from the first row. Without them, a single CREATE TABLE ... AS does the work.

A column that is NA in every row of a query (mutate(flag = NA)) has no type for DuckDB to infer, and the table stores it with the "NULL" type, which holds nothing but NULL until set_column_type() promotes it. Give the placeholder a type in the query (NA_character_, NA_real_) when the first values are known.

See also

Other table operations: add_data_files(), create_schema(), create_view(), drop_schema(), drop_view(), ducklake_exec(), get_ducklake_table(), get_metadata_table(), list_ducklake_tables(), replace_table(), show_ducklake_query()

Examples

lake_dir <- tempfile("create_lake_")
dir.create(lake_dir)
attach_ducklake("create_lake", lake_path = lake_dir)

# From data.frame
create_table(mtcars, "cars")

# From a local file
csv_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(mtcars, csv_path, row.names = FALSE)
create_table(csv_path, "cars_from_csv")

# From a lazy table: the query runs inside DuckDB and writes straight
# into the lake, without collecting into R
get_ducklake_table("cars") |>
  dplyr::filter(cyl > 4) |>
  create_table("big_cars")

# Partitioned, sorted, and compressed from the first load
create_table(
  mtcars, "cars_by_cyl",
  partition_by = "cyl", sort_by = "mpg DESC",
  options = list(parquet_compression = "zstd")
)
get_table_partitions("cars_by_cyl")
#>   schema_name  table_name partition_key_index column_name transform
#> 1        main cars_by_cyl                   0         cyl  identity

# From a URL -- needs network access and the httpfs extension
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
create_table("https://example.com/data.csv", "remote_table")
} # }

unlink(csv_path)

detach_ducklake("create_lake", shutdown = TRUE)
unlink(lake_dir, recursive = TRUE)
